en: The sun emits ultraviolet radiation that causes sunburns and skin damage, making daily sunscreen application essential for health.
When PAGASA raises Signal Number 2, winds reach 61 to 100 kilometers per hour, meaning you must stay indoors to avoid debris.
Floodwaters mix with sewage and chemicals, so you must wash your feet with soap to prevent leptospirosis bacteria from entering cuts.
During an earthquake, dropping to the ground, covering your head, and holding under a sturdy table prevents injuries from falling objects.
If the ocean water suddenly recedes far from the shore before a tsunami, you must immediately run to higher ground.
Root crops like sweet potatoes absorb harmful soil pollutants, so peeling and thoroughly washing them removes dirt and prevents stomach illnesses.
Pumice is a porous volcanic rock with a rough texture that safely scrubs dead skin off your heels during a bath.
The moon's gravity creates high tides that can cause dangerous rip currents, so always swim near a lifeguard during full moons.
Because lightning strikes the tallest objects, you should never stand under an isolated tree during a thunderstorm to avoid fatal electrocution.
Boiling drinking water for at least one minute kills harmful waterborne bacteria and viruses, preventing diseases like cholera and typhoid.
Heavy rains after a volcanic eruption mix with ash to form fast-flowing lahars, so avoid river valleys during storms.
A high heat index makes sweating less effective at cooling your body, so drinking plenty of water prevents dangerous heatstroke.
